title: Adaptive spillover token-bucket and latency-aware routing shim for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a spillover-aware token-bucket admission shim and routing policy for Dedicated fleets. Goal is to provide stable per-tenant throughput guarantees while enabling graceful overload shedding and low-latency fallbacks. The feature combines: (1) per-tenant token buckets with borrow/spillover lanes, (2) latency-aware demotion that moves requests to lower-cost/compatible model variants or queued slow-paths, and (3) a routing shim that routes spillover traffic to pre-warmed burst nodes or cross-region spare capacity according to policy. This ticket covers design, prototype, integration with the autoscaler, API flags, rollout plan, and observability dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant steady-state throughput guarantees honored for 95% of tenants under 90th percentile fleet utilization
Under sudden load spikes, 99% of critical-tier requests either get served within latency SLO or are routed to a documented fallback path (queued slow-path or model variant)
Autoscaler integration: when spillover lane consistently exceeds threshold for >2m, autoscaler scale-up is triggered and observed in dedicated pool metrics
Unit and integration tests cover token borrow, spillback, demotion, and routing decisions with deterministic simulators
Dashboard widgets: tenant-level token consumption, spillover volume, routing decisions, and demotion counts available in Console (beta)
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Initial writeup and motivation. Pitched approach in infra sync. Key tradeoffs: complexity of cross-tenant borrowing vs predictability; decision leaning towards bounded spillover lanes with hard caps.

2025-02-22 - Luca Martinez: Prototype of token-bucket with spill lanes implemented in local simulator. Early findings: naive borrow increases tail latency for donors; added per-donor backpressure and donor-priority weighting.
2025-02-28 - Priya Rao (SRE): Reviewed approach. Requested clearer failure modes and metrics. Suggested explicit circuit-breaker metric for farms that accept spillover to avoid cascading overload.
2025-03-03 - Design review (Cheng Yu): UX for Console needs a toggle for 'spillover-enabled' per-dedicated-pool and clear visualization of demoted requests; added mockups to Confluence.

2025-03-04 - Luca Martinez: Implemented routing shim to prefer warm-burst nodes and added policy to fall back to cross-region spare only after local capacity exhausted. Integration tests drafted (see PR).
2025-03-04 - QA note: Need to add deterministic replay tests for tenant mixes that include high-burst low-latency and steady high-throughput workloads.
notes: Design alternatives considered: (A) strict per-tenant hard quotas with request rejection — simplest but poor UX; (B) unbounded borrowing — good for tail coverage but risks noisy-neighbor tails; (C) bounded spillover with donor protections (chosen)
Key metrics to monitor post-rollout: tenant_throughput_guarantee_ok_ratio, spillover_requests_per_min, demotion_rate, donor_latency_99, scale_up_trigger_count

Rollout plan: start with internal dogfood cluster, enable 'spillover' flag for 10% of fleets, observe 2 weeks, then 50% with rollback window. Automated rollback on donor_latency_99 > baseline * 1.5 for >30m
Operational runbooks: steps to disable spillover per-pool, emergency draining of burst nodes, and invoking manual demotion policies
